correctness.rationale: For two entities, the selected \(a\)-th quotient exceeding the rival's next unselected quotient gives \(a<hp_A+1\), so upper quota cannot fail. One seat is trivial, and the three-entity/two-seat cell is excluded because two seats for \(A\) with \(p_A\le1/2\) would require \(p_A/2>\max(p_B,p_C)\ge(1-p_A)/2\). At \((3,3)\), a violation must allocate all three seats to one entity, giving exactly the displayed chamber; at \((4,2)\), both seats to one entity gives the second chamber. These facts establish coordinatewise minimality. The exact-rational verifier independently checks integer grids, divisor certificates, witness minimality and the two exact integrals, and the simplex integrations were independently recomputed as \(1/45\) and \(1/40\).

value.rationale: Upper-quota failure of Jefferson is classical, but its sharp onset is a natural structural boundary of a foundational apportionment method. The complete chambers, exact geometric incidence probabilities and minimal integer witnesses resolve the first two admissible cells rather than merely supplying another counterexample.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical note, textbook exercise or old apportionment computation may contain the same minimal-cell classification.

final_claim: For pure Jefferson/D'Hondt apportionment with positive shares and a strict quotient cutoff, the coordinatewise-minimal upper-quota failure cells are exactly \((s,h)=(3,3)\) and \((4,2)\); the two complete violation chambers have normalized simplex probabilities \(1/45\) and \(1/40\), and their unique least-total positive-integer witnesses are respectively \((4,1,1)\) and \((3,1,1,1)\) up to permutation.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed historical note, textbook exercise or old apportionment computation may contain the same minimal-cell classification.
The theorem excludes statutory minimum-seat constraints, zero-share entities and tied quotient cutoffs.
The probabilities refer to normalized Lebesgue measure on the share simplex, not empirical political frequencies.
